name: Ethiopia
summary: The only African country never colonised, with its own alphabet, calendar and church — rock-hewn churches at Lalibela, the Simien escarpment above four thousand metres, and the Danakil below sea level.

entries.caption: The Roof of Africa
entries.description: Eighty per cent of Africa's land above three thousand metres is in this one country.
entries.subject: the Simien mountains escarpment dropping away into cloud

entries.caption: Escarpment and Rift
entries.description: The Rift Valley cuts the whole country in half, with highlands either side of it.
entries.subject: the Ethiopian Rift valley lakes seen from the escarpment

entries.caption: Gelada and Walia Ibex
entries.description: The gelada lives nowhere else on earth, and grazes the Simien escarpment in troops of hundreds.
entries.subject: a troop of gelada baboons grazing on the Simien escarpment

entries.caption: Bale and the Ethiopian Wolf
entries.description: The Bale mountains hold the last five hundred Ethiopian wolves, on the Sanetti plateau.
entries.subject: an Ethiopian wolf on the Sanetti plateau in Bale

entries.caption: The Simiens
entries.description: Ras Dashen is 4,550 metres; the trek to it runs along the escarpment for days.
entries.subject: trekkers on the ridge trail in the Simien mountains

entries.caption: The Blue Nile Falls
entries.description: Tis Issat — the water that smokes — where the Blue Nile leaves Lake Tana.
entries.subject: the Blue Nile falls in full flow at Tis Issat

entries.caption: Lake Tana
entries.description: The source of the Blue Nile, with monasteries on its islands still in use.
entries.subject: an island monastery on Lake Tana seen from the water

entries.caption: No Coast, and No Loss
entries.description: Landlocked since 1993 — the water here is the Rift lakes and the crater lakes of Bishoftu.
entries.subject: a crater lake at Bishoftu in the early morning

entries.caption: Harenna and the Church Forests
entries.description: Harenna's cloud forest in Bale, and the church forests that are the last woodland of the north.
entries.subject: a round church surrounded by its own remnant forest

entries.caption: Trekking Country
entries.description: Multi-day treks in the Simiens and Bale, and the Danakil at a hundred metres below sea level.
entries.subject: the sulphur springs of the Danakil depression

entries.caption: Its Own Everything
entries.description: Its own alphabet, its own calendar with thirteen months, and its own church since the fourth century.
entries.subject: priests in white robes outside a rock-hewn church

entries.caption: Omo Valley
entries.description: The lower Omo holds sixteen peoples in one valley, and the visits should be arranged carefully.
entries.subject: a village of the lower Omo valley at the end of the day

entries.caption: Injera and Doro Wat
entries.description: Sourdough injera under everything, and fasting food that has made vegans of visitors.
entries.subject: injera with several wats served on a shared platter

entries.caption: Timkat and Meskel
entries.description: Timkat in January at Gondar, and Meskel bonfires across the country in September.
entries.subject: the Timkat procession with white-robed crowds at Gondar

entries.caption: Weaving and Silver
entries.description: Handwoven shemma cotton, and Coptic crosses in silver, each region with its own shape.
entries.subject: a silversmith working an Ethiopian cross

entries.caption: Lalibela
entries.description: Eleven churches cut down into solid rock in the twelfth century, still in use every day.
entries.subject: the rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis at Lalibela

entries.caption: Aksum and Gondar
entries.description: The Aksumite stelae, and the seventeenth-century castles of Gondar built by Fasilides.
entries.subject: the stone castles of Fasil Ghebbi at Gondar

entries.caption: Addis Ababa
entries.description: Founded 1886, at 2,355 metres, and the diplomatic capital of the continent.
entries.subject: the Merkato district of Addis Ababa from above

entries.caption: Round Houses and Rock Churches
entries.description: The tukul, and the rock architecture of Tigray cut into cliff faces you have to climb.
entries.subject: a Tigray rock church high in a cliff face

entries.caption: Coffee, Properly
entries.description: Coffee was found here, and it is still roasted, ground and poured in front of you.
entries.subject: a coffee ceremony with roasting pan and jebena

entries.caption: Highland Travel
entries.description: Cool highland air, short flights between the historic sites, and no malaria at altitude.
entries.subject: a family walking a highland track in northern Ethiopia

entries.caption: Trek and Climb
entries.description: The Simien traverse, Bale's plateau, and the Tigray churches that need a rope.
entries.subject: a climber on the approach to a Tigray cliff church

entries.caption: Lodges on the Escarpment
entries.description: Limalimo and Bale Mountain Lodge — small, sited well, and built by people who stayed.
entries.subject: a lodge terrace on the edge of the Simien escarpment

entries.caption: Community Conservation
entries.description: Guides and scouts drawn from the villages inside the parks, which is why the wolves are still there.
entries.subject: a park scout looking out over the Bale plateau

entries.caption: Faces and Escarpments
entries.description: The light at four thousand metres, and portraiture that has to be asked for properly.
entries.subject: cloud below the escarpment edge in the Simien mountains

entries.caption: Tigray
entries.description: Rock churches in cliff faces reached by hand and foot, with almost nobody else there.
entries.subject: the climb to a rock church in the Gheralta mountains

entries.caption: Nothing Else Like It
entries.description: No colonial period, its own script, its own calendar, and its own year that starts in September.
entries.subject: a priest holding a processional cross at a rock church
